hypothesis: Exact-C currently learns a four-class failure taxonomy and obtains success probability only by marginalizing that taxonomy. A direct binary CatBoost on the identical legal feature recipe can allocate all splits and categorical target statistics to the scored success-versus-failure boundary. Training only on historical R rows and routing only R predictions also avoids the known 2023 F regime break.

novelty_audit.prior_direct_binary: v3_cat_kp50_kpl50_Ronly tested a much smaller base+e14+platoon recipe only on 2024. It omitted exact-C hand/count/type-count cells, rich TrackMan history, and batter encoders, and was not a source-validated candidate.
novelty_audit.prior_r_specialist: v5_r_specialist_all/decay/recent3 retained the four-class catboost_outcome objective; it was not direct binary Logloss.
novelty_audit.prior_numeric_binary: v4_numeric_cat_ctxlvl_tm_rfit used ordinal numeric category encoding and a different feature/state recipe. This candidate preserves native CatBoost categorical CTRs and exact-C features.

parent.recipe: exact component C four-class outcome model

candidate.model: native categorical CatBoostClassifier with binary Logloss and BrierScore evaluation
candidate.routing: F rows remain exactly parent; only R rows receive the candidate blend
selection_order: maximize minimum full-score gain over 2020 and 2021
maximize minimum R-score gain over 2020 and 2021

source_protocol.on_fail: Close direct-binary exact-C without reading 2022+ candidate labels.
source_protocol.on_pass: Freeze gamma and run untouched 2022/2023 development validation.
